## `virtualization.hypervisor`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

A virtualization layer that manages one or more virtual machines. Analogous to a hypervisor in any cloud or on-premises virtualization environment.

**Type:** `virtualization.hypervisor`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |

| Identity | [`virtualization.hypervisor.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the hypervisor instance. [1] | `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| Description | [`virtualization.hypervisor.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the hypervisor. | `active`; `inactive`; `unknown` |
| Description | [`virtualization.hypervisor.type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The type of hypervisor controlling the virtual machines. [2] | `type1`; `type2`; `unknown` |
| Description | [`virtualization.hypervisor.version`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-hypervisor-version) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The version string of the hypervisor software. [3] | `6.4.0`; `2024.1.1`; `4.2.1-release` |
| Description | [`virtualization.system.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-system-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [4] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |

**[1] `virtualization.hypervisor.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this hypervisor instance within the virtualization platform.

**[2] `virtualization.hypervisor.type`:** Classifies the hypervisor by its position in the virtualization stack. Type-1 (bare-metal) hypervisors run directly on hardware; Type-2 (hosted) hypervisors run within a host operating system.

**[3] `virtualization.hypervisor.version`:** The version as reported by the hypervisor software itself. Format is hypervisor-specific and should be used for informational purposes and correlation with vendor release notes.

**[4] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the specific hypervisor or partitioning technology in use. This attribute allows consumers to correlate platform-specific behaviour and capabilities when multiple virtualization technologies are observed in a mixed environment. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.

## `virtualization.partition`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

A hardware or firmware enforced partition of a virtualization platform. Analogous to a virtual machine or cloud instance, but enforced at the firmware level rather than by a software hypervisor.

**Type:** `virtualization.partition`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |

| Identity | [`virtualization.partition.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the hardware or firmware partition. [5] | `0abc1234-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab`; `partition-3` |
| Identity | [`virtualization.platform.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-platform-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the virtualization platform. [6] | `CPC-9175-ME1-0001`; `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The human-readable name assigned to the partition. [7] | `LPAR1`; `PROD`; `LINUX01` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.number`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-number) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | int | The partition number assigned by the virtualization platform. [8] | `1`; `2`; `15` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the partition. [9] | `active`; `not_activated`; `stopped` |
| Description | [`virtualization.partition.type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The workload type or operational mode of the partition. [10] | `general_purpose`; `linux_only`; `ssc` |

**[5] `virtualization.partition.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this partition within its virtualization platform. On IBM Z in PR/SM (classic) mode this is the partition object-id assigned by the HMC.

**[6] `virtualization.platform.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this physical computing platform within its management domain. For IBM Z this corresponds to the CPC (Central Processing Complex) object-id as reported by the HMC Web Services API. Alignment with OTel base registry: this attribute is functionally equivalent to `host.id`. Consumers that understand the generic host entity should prefer `host.id`; use this attribute when the management domain requires the platform-internal UUID specifically. In virtualization.platform metrics, `virtualization.platform.id` is used as the time-series discriminating attribute because the identity attribute of the `virtualization.platform` entity is `host.name` and the UUID is needed to uniquely identify the entity instance when metrics are aggregated across platforms with different name scopes.

**[7] `virtualization.partition.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface, e.g., the HMC (Hardware Management Console) for IBM Z PR/SM partitions. On IBM Z, partition names are 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters.

**[8] `virtualization.partition.number`:** The numeric index identifying the partition within the platform. On IBM Z PR/SM (classic) mode, this corresponds to the LPAR number as reported by the HMC Web Services API.

**[9] `virtualization.partition.state`:** Reflects the current activation or execution state of the partition as reported by the virtualization platform management interface.

**[10] `virtualization.partition.type`:** Classifies the partition by the category of workload it is configured to run. On IBM Z, this maps to the partition type field on the HMC.

**[11] `host.name`:** The name of the physical computing platform as configured in the platform management interface. For IBM Z systems this is the CPC name as configured on the Hardware Management Console (HMC). Consumers using the generic host entity should use host.name as the primary identifier; virtualization.platform.id may be used as an additional opaque UUID where required.

**[12] `host.arch`:** The CPU architecture of the platform. SHOULD be set to "s390x" for IBM Z and LinuxONE systems.

**[13] `host.id`:** A platform-specific opaque UUID that uniquely identifies this physical platform within its management domain. For IBM Z this corresponds to the CPC object-id as reported by the HMC Web Services API. Consumers that use only the generic host entity should prefer host.id over virtualization.platform.id.

**[14] `host.type`:** The hardware model of the physical platform. For IBM Z systems this is the machine type and model concatenated with a hyphen, e.g., "9175-ME1" for the IBM z16 Model ME1. Consumers that use only the generic host entity should prefer host.type over virtualization.platform.model.

**[15] `virtualization.platform.firmware.version`:** The firmware or microcode version as reported by the platform management interface. For IBM Z this corresponds to the driver or MCL level reported by the HMC. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.

**[16] `virtualization.platform.id`:** An opaque platform-specific identifier that uniquely identifies this physical computing platform. Prefer host.id for cross-platform compatibility; use this attribute when the management domain requires the platform-internal UUID.

**[17] `virtualization.platform.serial_number`:** The hardware serial number as reported by the platform management interface. Supplements host.id for platforms where the serial number and the management UUID differ.

**[18] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the specific hypervisor or partitioning technology managing this platform (e.g. ibm.prsm, ibm.zvm, vmware.esxi).

**[19] `virtualization.platform.model`:** The model identifier of the platform hardware. Consumers should prefer host.type; this attribute is retained for implementations that need the platform-specific model string separately.

**[20] `virtualization.platform.name`:** The human-readable name as configured in the platform management interface. Consumers should prefer host.name as the primary name attribute; this attribute is retained for compatibility with implementations that populate both.

## `virtualization.vm`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

A virtual machine managed by a hypervisor. Analogous to an EC2 instance, a Google Compute Engine VM, or any cloud instance in distributed systems observability.

**Type:** `virtualization.vm`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |

[21] | `vm-0abc1234`; `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| Description | [`virtualization.vm.cpu.count`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-cpu-count) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | int | The number of virtual CPUs (vCPUs) allocated to the virtual machine. [22] | `1`; `2`; `4`; `8` |
| Description | [`virtualization.vm.instance_id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-instance-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The cloud or platform provider's instance identifier for the virtual machine. [23] | `i-0abc123def456789`; `1234567890abcdef0` |
| Description | [`virtualization.vm.machine_type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-machine-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The machine type or hardware profile assigned to the virtual machine. [24] | `n1-standard-2`; `t3.medium`; `9175-ME1` |
| Description | [`virtualization.vm.memory.size`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-memory-size) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | int | The amount of memory allocated to the virtual machine, in mebibytes (MiB). [25] | `1024`; `4096`; `16384` |
| Description | [`virtualization.vm.name`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The human-readable name assigned to the virtual machine. [26] | `my-web-server`; `prod-db-01`; `test-vm` |
| Description | [`virtualization.vm.nested_virtualization.enabled`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-nested-virtualization-enabled) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | boolean | Indicates whether nested virtualization is enabled on this virtual machine. [27] | |
| Description | [`virtualization.vm.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-vm-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the virtual machine. | `running`; `stopped`; `paused` |

**[21] `virtualization.vm.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this virtual machine within the hypervisor. Analogous to `host.id` for physical machines or a container ID for containers.

**[22] `virtualization.vm.cpu.count`:** The number of virtual CPUs visible to the guest operating system. This may differ from the number of physical CPUs on the underlying host.

**[23] `virtualization.vm.instance_id`:** A provider-assigned instance identifier, distinct from the hypervisor's own identifier (`virtualization.vm.id`). For example, on AWS this would be the EC2 instance ID; on IBM Z HMC DPM mode it would be the partition object-id.

**[24] `virtualization.vm.machine_type`:** A string identifying the virtual machine's hardware configuration class as defined by the hypervisor or cloud provider. For IBM Z DPM partitions this corresponds to the partition type profile.

**[25] `virtualization.vm.memory.size`:** The total memory allocation visible to the guest operating system, expressed in mebibytes (MiB). This is the configured allocation, not necessarily the currently consumed amount.

**[26] `virtualization.vm.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface. Names are not guaranteed to be unique across hypervisors; use `virtualization.vm.id` for unambiguous identification.

**[27] `virtualization.vm.nested_virtualization.enabled`:** When `true`, the virtual machine is configured to expose virtualization extensions to its guest operating system, allowing a hypervisor to run inside the VM. Not all hypervisors or platforms support this capability.

| `failed` | Virtual machine has encountered a fatal error and cannot recover without operator intervention. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `migrating` | Virtual machine is being live-migrated to another host without interruption. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `paused` | Virtual machine is suspended with state preserved in memory. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `running` | Virtual machine is running and processing workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `scheduled` | Virtual machine has been assigned to a host node and is being prepared to start. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `scheduling` | Virtual machine has been requested but is waiting for the scheduler to assign it to a host node. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `stopped` | Virtual machine is stopped and not consuming CPU resources. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `succeeded` | Virtual machine completed its workload and terminated cleanly (applicable to batch or ephemeral VMs). | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | Virtual machine state is not known or cannot be determined. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
